concepts.def: Reformer whose Report on the Sanitary Condition linked poverty, disease and slum housing, prompting 1848 Public Health Act.
First national public health legislation creating General Board of Health; permissive not compulsory, limited impact.
Hot summer when Thames sewage caused parliament to recess; led to Bazalgette's London sewer system.
Compulsory Act forcing councils to provide clean water, drainage and sewers; passed under Disraeli's government.
Welfare measures including school meals, old age pensions (1908) and National Insurance Act (1911) under Asquith.
National Health Service founded by Aneurin Bevan providing free healthcare at point of use, funded by taxation.
